name: Proxmox_VE_Node_StoragePools
description: Size, use and health of this Proxmox VE node's ZFS pools, LVM volume groups and LVM thin pools, asked of the node itself.
technicalNotes:
BatchScript: three calls to this node per interval, /nodes/{node}/disks/zfs, /disks/lvm and /disks/lvmthin. Requires Sys.Audit on /, which the PVEAuditor role includes. A node without one kind -- no ZFS installed -- answers an error for it; that kind is skipped. A node that cannot be reached fails the run, so its instances are kept.

The pools are what Proxmox stores sit on: a zfspool store on a ZFS pool, an lvmthin store on a thin pool, which sits in a volume group, an lvm store on a volume group. Proxmox_VE_Cluster_StorageCapacity reports the store; this module the pool beneath it, including what the store does not show -- a ZFS pool's health and fragmentation, a thin pool's metadata use, which stops every write in the pool when it fills.

Wildvalues are the pool's kind and name: zfs/<pool>, lvm/<vg>, lvmthin/<vg>/<lv>.

Healthy is reported for ZFS pools only, 1 when the pool is ONLINE; DEGRADED, FAULTED or any other state is 0. FragmentationPercent is ZFS's own figure. MetadataUsedPercent is reported for thin pools only.

Each instance carries a topology vertex for Proxmox_VE_Cluster_Topology (predef.externalResourceID and predef.externalResourceType). The keys are written plain, so where topo.namespace or topo.blacklist is set, which rewrites the TopologySource's keys, discovery stamps none: the instances stay, off the map. The vertex is type StorageAggregate, drawn between the store and the node's disks.

Applies on ProxmoxVE_Node resources the NetScan has not marked unreachable (pve.netscan.reachable). The node is asked directly, at this resource's own hostname, and never through another node: another node would answer for itself. The suite has no addCategory_* PropertySource: the NetScan sets the categories and pve.cluster.role, and the product page lists them for a resource added by hand.

Units: sizes in GB. MB and GB are decimal (10^6 and 10^9 bytes); the product page states the suite's convention.

datapoints.name: UsedGB
datapoints.description: Space allocated in the pool, GB (decimal, 10^9 bytes).

datapoints.name: FreeGB
datapoints.description: Space free in the pool, GB (decimal, 10^9 bytes).

datapoints.name: UsedPercent
datapoints.alertBody:
Storage pool ##INSTANCE## on ##HOST## is ##VALUE##% full. A full thin pool or ZFS pool stops writes for every guest on it.

This started at ##START##, ##DURATION## ago.

datapoints.name: Healthy
datapoints.description: ZFS pools only: 1 when the pool is ONLINE, 0 in any other state (DEGRADED, FAULTED, UNAVAIL, ...).
datapoints.alertBody:
ZFS pool ##INSTANCE## on ##HOST## is not ONLINE: a device in it has failed or is missing. Check zpool status on the node.

Status: ##ALERTVALUEDISPLAYSTATUSNAME## (##VALUE##).

This started at ##START##, ##DURATION## ago.

datapoints.name: FragmentationPercent
datapoints.description: ZFS pools only: free-space fragmentation, percent, as zpool reports it.

datapoints.name: MetadataUsedPercent
datapoints.description: LVM thin pools only: metadata space used, percent. A thin pool whose metadata fills stops every write in the pool.
datapoints.alertBody:
LVM thin pool ##INSTANCE## on ##HOST## has used ##VALUE##% of its metadata space. When it fills, every write to every volume in the pool fails. Extend the metadata volume (lvextend --poolmetadatasize).

This started at ##START##, ##DURATION## ago.
